notes.decision: Rendered as 'mingled' — Lycopolitan qualitative likely from ⲱⲧⲉ/ⲧⲱϩ 'mix, mingle.' Fits the triadic series 'defiled, heaped together, mingled' describing Sin's confused forms.
Greek φορεῖν 'wear, bear (clothing)' — rendered 'donned' to capture the sense of Sin putting on Error and Forgetfulness as garments.
Lycopolitan ⲃⲱⲉ = Sah. ⲃϣⲉ 'forgetfulness'; capitalized as cosmic principle paired with Error (ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ).
ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱⲃⲱ 'do/make forgetting' = 'forget'. The triad substance/kind/manner echoes the established vocabulary triad (ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ + ⲅⲉⲛⲟⲥ + ⲣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ).
Rendered 'dwelling-place' — Lycopolitan compound ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄- + verbal element from ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'dwell, settle.' The 'door of his dwelling' is the way back to the Father.

The structural pattern lines 13-21 follows: ϣⲁϩⲧⲟⲩⲱ (he raises) + faculty + ⲛϩⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (releasing it from) + body-part; then ⲛ̄ϩⲙⲟⲩⲣ (and binds) + Sin's counterpart-faculty in the body-part. Five faculties paired with five body-parts: mind/bone, thought/sinew, teaching/vein, counsel/flesh, reflection/skin.
Rendered 'sinew' (Sah. ⲙⲟⲩⲧ); paired with ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'thought' as the second faculty/body-part pair.
Rendered 'vein' — Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲙⲉ 'vein, channel.' Paired with ⲧⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching' as third faculty/body-part pair.
Rendered 'skin' (Sah. ϣⲁⲁⲣ); paired with ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ 'reflection' as fifth faculty/body-part pair.
Lycopolitan ⲧⲍⲉ = Sah. ⲧϩⲉ 'manner, way.' Standard summary formula: 'This is the manner in which...'
Conjunctive 'and they (become) free' — ⲣⲙ̄ⲍⲉ = freeman/free (per accumulated vocabulary). The soul's faculties are made free from Sin's parallel members.
Imperfect with qualitative ⲃⲏⲩ from ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' = 'which had gone forth' — referring to Sin's five members that had emerged into the body.
'New Man' — ⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ = 'man of newness'; the regenerated soul-construct fashioned by the Savior. Standard Manichaean technical term.
ⲡⲛⲉⲩ = ⲡⲛⲁⲩ 'the hour'; ⲁⲉ = δέ. Temporal connector: 'And the hour in which he will mold and fashion and refine the New Man, then he brings forth...'
Identifying gloss: the mind = love (ἀγάπη). Begins the explicit mapping of the five faculties to five virtues placed in the New Man (mind=love, thought=faith, teaching=perfection).
Lycopolitan ⲛⲁⲍⲧⲉ = Sah. ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'faith.' Maps to the second faculty (thought).
Reading 'the teaching' — ⲧⲉϩ likely a Lycopolitan article variant, or fem possessive ⲧⲉϥ→ⲧⲉϩ. Following the pattern, teaching is the third faculty mapped to ⲡⲭⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'perfection/completion.'

proposed_terms.rationale: Lycopolitan compound ⲙⲁ-ⲛ- + verbal element related to ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'to dwell, settle.' The phrase 'door of the ⲙⲁⲛⲱⲩⲗⲏⲩ' parallels well-known Manichaean expressions for the abode of light/the Father.
Lycopolitan ⲕⲉⲥ = Sahidic ⲕⲁⲥ 'bone.' First in the body-parts series paired with mind.
Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲧ 'sinew, tendon.' Second body-part paired with thought.
Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲙⲉ 'vein/channel.' Third body-part paired with teaching.
Lycopolitan ϣⲁⲣⲉ = Sahidic ϣⲁⲁⲣ 'skin.' Fifth body-part paired with reflection.
ⲭⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'fulfill, complete' nominalized — the third virtue in the New Man series, paired with ⲧⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching.' Captures the ascetic-soteriological sense of bringing the work to its end.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sah. ⲃϣⲉ 'forgetfulness.' Capitalized as cosmic principle, paired with Error (ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ) as garments donned by Sin.
Verbal noun used with ⲣ̄- 'do/make' to mean 'forget.' ⲁⲥⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲱⲃⲱ = 'she forgot.'
